note: Built only from works cited in project/paper.txt / project/README_1.md, characterized via the citing paper's own description (no web access this run; see source_registry.json verification fields).

matrix.key_assumption: query/document relevance is well approximated by token overlap + frequency statistics
matrix.strength: simple, no training data needed, used here as the zero-shot reference point
matrix.weakness_limit: lexical gap: cannot match semantically related but lexically different text (SRC-002)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: the baseline the whole benchmark is compared against

matrix.problem_framing: lexical mismatch between query and answer wording
matrix.strength: names the lexical-gap problem that motivates neural retrieval
matrix.weakness_limit: predates neural methods; does not itself propose a fix used here
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: motivates why neural retrieval was pursued at all (Introduction)

matrix.key_assumption: masked-language-model pre-training transfers to downstream tasks via fine-tuning
matrix.data_eval: GLUE and related NLP benchmarks (not IR-specific)
matrix.strength: strong transferable representations, foundation for nearly every neural system evaluated
matrix.weakness_limit: not itself a retrieval model; retrieval-specific adaptation is the object of the method family rows below
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: shared backbone of DPR, ANCE, TAS-B, DeepCT, SPARTA, ColBERT, and the BM25+CE cross-encoder

matrix.key_assumption: a single dense embedding per query/document, trained with in-batch + hard negatives, suffices for relevance matching
matrix.data_eval: open-domain QA datasets (NQ, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, CuratedTREC)
matrix.weakness_limit: trained only on QA data, not MS MARCO; generalizes worst of the 10 systems tested in this paper
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: one of the 5 architecture families evaluated; the weakest zero-shot generalizer (C010)

matrix.key_assumption: negatives mined from an up-to-date approximate nearest-neighbor index are more informative than random/in-batch negatives
matrix.strength: improves over earlier dense retrievers in-domain
matrix.weakness_limit: still underperforms BM25 on average zero-shot (C006); prefers longer retrieved documents than TAS-B (C014)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: dense baseline compared against TAS-B throughout Section 5 and Appendix H

matrix.key_assumption: balanced topic-aware batch sampling plus Margin-MSE distillation from stronger teacher models yields a better training signal than in-batch negatives alone
matrix.strength: best zero-shot generalization among the dense models tested here (C012)
matrix.weakness_limit: still net-negative vs. BM25 on average (-2.8%); prefers shorter retrieved documents, costly on 2 datasets (C014)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: the strongest dense baseline; basis for the GenQ domain-adaptation experiment

matrix.key_assumption: token-level embeddings with a lightweight max-similarity aggregation capture more nuance than a single pooled vector, without the full cost of cross-attention
matrix.strength: one of the two best-generalizing architectures on average (+2.5%)
matrix.weakness_limit: still fails to beat BM25 on 9 of 18 datasets; largest index footprint of any system tested (C007, C011)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: one of the 5 architecture families; illustrates the accuracy/index-size trade-off

matrix.problem_framing: improving a first-stage ranking with a second, more expensive pass
matrix.key_assumption: jointly encoding the query and document with cross-attention, for a short candidate list only, captures relevance signal a bi-encoder cannot
matrix.strength: large accuracy gains over first-stage rankers
matrix.weakness_limit: high computational overhead (only feasible on a short re-ranking list)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: basis for the BM25+CE system, the best zero-shot generalizer overall but the slowest (C007, C011)

matrix.problem_framing: closing the lexical gap without abandoning an inverted index
matrix.key_assumption: a sequence-to-sequence model can predict plausible queries for a document, and appending them adds retrievable vocabulary
matrix.strength: one of the few non-lexical systems that beats BM25 on a majority of BEIR datasets (11/18)
matrix.weakness_limit: still a lexical-index method underneath; gains are vocabulary-level, not representation-level
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: contrasts with the term-weighting sparse methods (DeepCT, SPARTA), which fail to generalize (C009)

matrix.problem_framing: compressing large Transformers without losing task accuracy
matrix.key_assumption: deep self-attention distillation preserves most of a larger model's behavior in a much smaller network
matrix.strength: lets the best-generalizing re-ranker run with a comparatively small cross-encoder
matrix.weakness_limit: still the most latency-costly system in this paper's efficiency comparison (C007)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: identifies the specific cross-encoder used inside BM25+CE

matrix.key_assumption: testing across 8 QA datasets is enough to assess cross-domain retrieval generalization
matrix.data_eval: 8 QA datasets, 5 of which are Wikipedia-based; mostly under 100k candidate sentences
matrix.strength: first cross-domain look at answer retrieval generalization
matrix.weakness_limit: one task only, mostly small/Wikipedia corpora -- does not test cross-task or larger-corpus generalization
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: establishes the GAP this paper targets (C002)

matrix.key_assumption: a shared Wikipedia snapshot is a sufficient retrieval source for all 5 task types
matrix.strength: broad task-type coverage for knowledge-intensive NLP
matrix.weakness_limit: retrieval is secondary to the end task and always Wikipedia-only -- does not test retrieval generalization across domains
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: second source establishing the GAP this paper targets (C002)

matrix.problem_framing: building a usable IR test collection under a fast-moving pandemic literature
matrix.key_assumption: pooling top hits from many participating systems approximates a complete relevance judgment set
matrix.strength: one of the few BEIR collections built by pooling many, architecturally diverse, systems
matrix.weakness_limit: pooling from mostly-lexical participating systems can still miss non-lexical systems' unique hits, as this paper's own case study shows (C018-C019)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: the dataset used for the annotation-bias case study

matrix.problem_framing: reproducibility and interpretability of BEIR-style multi-dataset comparisons
matrix.key_assumption: single-number averages across heterogeneous datasets obscure meaningful model differences that effect-size analysis can recover
matrix.strength: reproducible reference implementations and per-dataset effect sizes
matrix.weakness_limit: a 2024 follow-up, so not part of the systems/analysis in this paper itself
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: a caveat on how to read this paper's own averaged comparisons (used in Discussion/Limitations)

matrix.key_assumption: Bing search logs plus human-selected relevant passages approximate real retrieval demand at scale
matrix.strength: large enough to fine-tune modern neural retrievers
matrix.weakness_limit: single domain/style of query and document; a system tuned only on it may not generalize (this paper's central question)
matrix.relation_to_this_paper: the in-domain training/reference dataset for the paper's headline in-domain-vs-zero-shot comparison

dimensions_selected_for_related_work: method family (lexical / sparse-neural / dense / late-interaction / re-ranking) -- explains the architecture-level results
scope of prior multi-dataset benchmarks (single task vs. broad; Wikipedia-only vs. diverse) -- explains why the GAP exists
